description.text: Sets the vertex color. Connect a BlendMat node to the particle input of this node to blend this node's color with texture input to the BlendMat node. If the color from texture option is enabled, this color is ignored. It will also be ignored if you're using geometry as the particle representation.

The vertex colors of the particles will take their initial colour from the colour of the emitter geometry texture at that point. The colour will modulate as the texture changes.

This will be ignored if you're using geometry as the particle representation.
How to draw in 3D preview.  The viewer can override this setting.

Identifies the channels that the particles will be in. By default, the particles from each emitter are present in the A channel only. You can have multiple emitters emitting particles into different channels, and particle force nodes affecting different channels.
Specify where the particles should be emitted from on the geometry when the geometry input is in use.  Points, edges, faces or bbox.

Randomly - chooses a random point within a face. The random seed is always the same.
Uniformly - particles are emitted from every vertex on every frame. This ignores the emission rate setting.
In order - particles are emitted from the vertices of the geometry input in ascending order.
Allows you to import transformation data from an external file or export existing transformation data to an external file
Transform Data

This determines whether the particle representations animate after emission.  If "constant", then they do not animate, and keep the same representation for their entire lifetime.  If "in steps", then the representation advances frame by frame.  If "randomly", then a different random frame is picked each time.

Setting a half-life will make a fraction of particles die randomly each frame such that on average half of the particles that existed at a given time will continue to exist after the half-life (as per radioactive decay). After twice this time, only a quarter of the original particles will be left, etc.

This knob determines which "particles" input will be used for the representation. If it is "randomly", then a random input will be picked for each particle.  Otherwise, if it is "in order", the inputs will be cycled through.
The number of frames that each particle will exist for.

A channel of the input geometry texture which is used to modulate the lifetime. For example, if you are emitting from a Card which has a Ramp texture, particles emitted from the light parts of the ramp (values closer to 1) will have a lifetime value closer to that set in the max lifetime than particles emitted from the dark parts (values closer to 0).

Produces a random variation in the max lifetime value. Adds a Gaussian-distributed random number to the value multiplied by the variation value. Roughly, setting variation to 1 produces random numbers between 0 and  2*value, with a bell-shaped distribution around "value" 
0 means it's the number it's meant to be, 1 means it's very random.
Each particle has a mass which only comes into play when a force is applied.

A channel of the input geometry texture which is used to modulate the mass. For example, if you are emitting from a Card which has a Ramp texture, the particles from the light part of the Ramp (values closer to 1) will have a higher mass value (based on a percentage of the set 'mass' value) than from the dark parts (values closer to 0). Its a way of taking the input geometry and getting it to emit particles with different mass from different areas.

Produces a random variation in the mass value. Adds a Gaussian-distributed random number to the value multiplied by the variation value. Roughly, setting variation to 1 produces random numbers between 0 and  2*value, with a bell-shaped distribution around "value" 
0 means it's the number it's meant to be, 1 means it's very random.
The Local matrix applies a matrix to this op relative to the transformation of the input op.
The number of frames that will be used in animation from the particle input.
Pivot Rotate
Pivot Translate

Determines how the initial particle velocity directions are randomized. 
Not random - Directions are not randomized. The emit object's normals are used to determine direction
Randomized - The initial directions are completely randomized.
Randomized outwards - The initial directions are randomized but will always move either away from the centre of the 
object (when emit_order is set to bbox), or at no more than 90 degrees from the nearest point normal (when emit_order 
is set to all other values.

The number of particles emitted per frame. It is an exact number, not an average. It will decrease if you change the probability. It is affected by the setting of the rate channel: if your rate channel is not at a value of 1 all the way through, the emission rate would be less.

A channel of the input geometry texture which is used to modulate the rate. For example, if you are emitting from a Card which has a Ramp texture, it will emit more particles from the light part of the Ramp (values closer to 1) than from the dark parts (values closer to 0). Its a way of taking the input geometry and getting it to emit from certain places.

Produces a random variation in the emission rate value. Adds a Gaussian-distributed random number to the value multiplied by the variation value. Roughly, setting variation to 1 produces random numbers between 0 and  2*value, with a bell-shaped distribution around "value" 
0 means it's the number it's meant to be, 1 means it's very random.
The shape within which particles will be affected by this op.
If checked, particles outside the region will be affected rather than those inside it.
Sets how the object will render.  Independent from the OpenGL preview selection.
Specifies the order to apply Euler angles to the rotation.
Rotate

Particles have an orientation in 3D space and they spin around their local y-axis according to the rotation velocity. 
The y-axis points in the direction the particles were initially emitted, unless a ParticleMotionAlign node is used to align them along their current direction of motion.

A channel of the input geometry texture which is used to modulate the speed of rotation. For example, if you are emitting from a Card which has a Ramp texture, the rotation velocity of the particles emitted from the light part of the Ramp (values closer to 1) will be greater than that of those emitted from the dark parts (values closer to 0).

Produces a random variation in the rotation velocity value. Adds a Gaussian-distributed random number to the value multiplied by the variation value. Roughly, setting variation to 1 produces random numbers between 0 and  2*value, with a bell-shaped distribution around "value" 
0 means it's the number it's meant to be, 1 means it's very random.
Scale

Used for anything that needs random numbers, in particular the probability. Its also used for things like the 'range' knobs in the emitter. You can achieve slightly different effects by changing the seed number.
Turn off to prevent picking with the mouse in the viewer.
If this is set to true, only points selected (with a preceding GeoSelect node) will be used as emission sites.

If selection_only is set to true and emit_from is set to something other than point, then this indicates the threshold used for selection testing. For example, if set to 0.5 then the boundary will be exactly halfway between selected and unselected points.
The size of each particle. If the representation input is geometry, the instance of that geometry at each particle will be affected by this value.

A channel of the input geometry texture which is used to modulate the size of the particles. For example, if you are emitting from a Card which has a Ramp texture, the size of the particles emitted from the light part of the Ramp (values closer to 1) will be greater than that of those emitted from the dark parts (values closer to 0).

Produces a random variation in the size value. Adds a Gaussian-distributed random number to the value multiplied by the variation value. Roughly, setting variation to 1 produces random numbers between 0 and  2*value, with a bell-shaped distribution around "value"
0 means it's the number it's meant to be, 1 means it's very random.
Skew

Set your geometry or pivot location to that of a selection within the scene
  • Geo to selection (position): sets the position of your geometry to the selection within the scene
  • Geo to selection (position, orientation): sets the position and orientation of your geometry to the selection within the scene
  • Geo to selection (position, orientation, size): sets the position, orientation and size of your geometry to the selection within the scene
  • Pivot to selection (position): sets the pivot position to the selection within the scene
  • Pivot to selection (orientation): sets the pivot orientation to the selection within the scene
  • Pivot to selection (position, orientation): sets the pivot position and orientation to the selection within the scene
Snap
Applies a spread to the particles. By default it forms a cone shape around the direction of emission.

Allows you to do a pre-roll with the particle system. For example, you might not want your particles to start at time zero, you might have wanted it to have had a chance to spread the particles out. You want the snow to already be there... not see the first snowflakes falling.

This knob determines the frame at which a newly emitted particle's representation starts from the selected input. If "first", it picks the first frame from the input for each new particle. If "in order", it picks successive frames for each new particle. If "current", it picks the frame that the particle was emitted. If "random", it picks a random frame within the representation's frame range.

This forces particle start frames to be within the range of the representation input, causing the "in order" and "current" options to wrap round back to the start of the frame range once it has been exceeded, in a loop.If the input is geometry with an animated texture, then you may need to add a FrameRange node as the default frame range for geometry is 1-1.
Transfers any velocity that the initial emitter has to the particles.
Time in frames to look forward and backward to determine the velocity.
Translate
Uniform Scale

Enable this option to manually specify all of the values for the local matrix applied to this op, or to expression link the local matrix to another op's matrix. Enabling this option disables the individual knobs above.
Speed in units per frame of the particles as they leave the emitter.

A channel of the input geometry texture which is used to modulate the velocity. For example, if you are emitting from a Card which has a Ramp texture, it will emit particles from the light parts of the ramp at a higher velocity (values closer to 1) than from the dark parts (values closer to 0).

Produces a random variation in the velocity value. Adds a Gaussian-distributed random number to the value multiplied by the variation value. Roughly, setting variation to 1 produces random numbers between 0 and  2*value, with a bell-shaped distribution around "value" 
0 means it's the number it's meant to be, 1 means it's very random.

The number of particles emitted per vertex per frame. It is an exact number, not an average. It will decrease if you change the probability. It is affected by the setting of the rate channel: if your rate channel is not at a value of 1 all the way through, the emission rate would be less.

Specifies the order to apply the transformations in. Options are:
SRT	Scale/Rotation/Translation
SRT	Scale/Translation/Rotation
RST	Rotation/Scale/Translation
RTS	Rotation/Translation/Scale
TSR	Translation/Scale/Rotation
TRS	Translation/Rotation/Scale

description.plain_text: Emits particles along the normal to the geometry. In the case of having no geometry input, the normal is the y-axis. Emit - the geometry from which the particles are emitted. Particle - either an image (in the case of a sprite) or some 3D geometry. Sprites are billboard images that always face the Camera square on. Merge - input existing particle streams.
description.text:
Emits particles along the normal to the geometry. In the case of having no geometry input, the normal is the y-axis. 
Emit - the geometry from which the particles are emitted. 
Particle - either an image (in the case of a sprite) or some 3D geometry. Sprites are billboard images that always face the Camera square on. 
Merge - input existing particle streams.
